clue.text: Newspaper feature a lot of care goes into

definitions.text: Newspaper feature a lot of care goes into

parts.words: Newspaper feature a lot of care goes into
parts.note: read as a column into which great anguish (a lot of care) is poured: readers' troubles sent to an advice page

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature that has been laboured over with great care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of care' looks like diligence, but here care means worry or distress, which pours into an advice column of readers' woes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the newspaper page where readers' personal problems are printed and answered by an advice writer.

clue.text: Discharge a Roman, initially

parts.note: Roman Catholic is abbreviated to its initials RC

explanation.surface: A Roman is the first to be released.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman stands for Roman Catholic, written RC by its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical discharge jumping a gap forms a luminous bridge of current, as in welding.

clue.text: One has something new or reconstructed

indicators.note: reconstructed means built again in a different form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone possesses an item that is either new or rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reconstructed' rearranges the letters of 'new or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is a person in possession of something.

clue.text: Person who works on railway as a detective?

definitions.meaning: a railway worker employed in a goods or marshalling yard
playfully, a man from Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters

explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, so the question mark lets a 'Yard man' be one of its detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway employee working in the sidings handles shunting, and a Scotland Yard officer is playfully the same word.

clue.text: Credit taken for advert's make-up

indicators.note: make-up is read as the way something is composed, so the letters are put together afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: Someone takes out a loan to pay for an advertisement's design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' rearranges FOR and ADVERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowing past a zero balance from a bank account is credit extended by the bank, here drawn on.

clue.text: Complete absence of parking in front of golf club

indicators.note: absence of means the word for parking is missing from the club

parts.note: a putter is a golf club used on the green
P is the map symbol for parking

explanation.surface: Total lack of parking spaces outside the golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absence of' drops P from PUTTER; 'in front of' tells you where P was.
explanation.definitionFit: Total or absolute, as in 'complete nonsense', is an adjectival sense of the word.

clue.text: Poem entering new level is more stylish

indicators.note: entering signals that the poem goes inside the combination of the other two pieces

parts.note: a tier is a level or layer
If is Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: A poem joining a new level is classier.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's 'If—' is the crossword poem; 'entering' puts IF into N + TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarter or neater is the comparative of a word meaning stylish or deft.

clue.text: Valueless thing nearly all present returned

indicators.note: returned signals that the shortened word is turned round and read backwards
nearly all means the word for present loses its final letter

parts.note: a present is a gift

explanation.surface: Someone receives a worthless present and sends it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly all' trims GIFT to GIF, and 'returned' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Not caring a fig means not caring at all: a fig is a trifle of no value.

clue.text: Face row in scene of conflict

parts.note: the front of something is its face
a line is a row

explanation.surface: Confronting a quarrel in a war zone.
explanation.walkthrough: Row reads as a quarrel but means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The forward edge of a battle zone, where opposing forces meet, is the battlefront.

clue.text: Epicurean who sees stars after midnight?

indicators.note: after means the stargazer piece comes behind the midnight letter

parts.note: the middle of the word night is its letter G
a stargazing scientist observes the stars

explanation.surface: A gourmet who sees stars after a late night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midnight' is the middle of 'night', G; 'after' puts the stargazer behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur of fine food, a gourmet, is someone devoted to the pleasures of eating.

clue.text: Agreeing such figures are undistinguished?

definitions.meaning: agreeing means in accord or consistent
in geometry, shapes of identical size and form cannot be told apart, so they are undistinguished

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: two shapes that match exactly in size and shape are indistinguishable from each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in accord or consistent with something is a standard meaning, and in geometry the word describes identical shapes.

clue.text: Rough silk — from its mill?

definitions.meaning: rough silk is the coarse silk fibre on the outside of a cocoon
George Eliot's novel The Mill on the ... names the river beside the mill, so the river is what the mill stands on

explanation.walkthrough: The second half alludes to George Eliot's novel 'The Mill on the Floss': the mill belongs to the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse silk fibres from the outside of a cocoon, used for embroidery thread, carry this name.

clue.text: Masonry containing secret passages

parts.note: read as a description of an Egyptian royal tomb of stone blocks with hidden inner corridors

explanation.surface: A stone wall with secret tunnels inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: Masonry suggests a wall or a Freemasons' lodge, but think of the great Egyptian tombs with hidden shafts.
explanation.definitionFit: Egyptian royal tombs of stacked stone blocks famously hold concealed corridors and chambers.

clue.text: Through money, a financial centre can show staying power

parts.note: per means through or by means of
tin is British slang for money
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: A financial hub shows resilience by means of its money.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is old British slang for cash; the City is London's banking district.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn persistence or tenacity is the ability to keep going, which is staying power.

clue.text: Push the boat out to find right seafood, say

indicators.note: say signals that the seafood word is taken only as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: an oyster is a kind of seafood

explanation.surface: Celebrating lavishly by going in search of the right seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Push the boat out' is a British idiom for celebrating extravagantly; the sound of OYSTER gives OISTER after R.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel noisily and extravagantly is to celebrate without restraint, which is what the idiom means.

clue.text: He makes the most of investment

indicators.note: the most of means nearly all of the word is kept, so its final letter goes

parts.note: investment can mean ceremonial dressing in robes, which is robing

explanation.surface: Someone who gets the best return from his investments.
explanation.walkthrough: Investment here is the act of clothing someone in robes of office (robing), not putting money to work; 'the most of' drops the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's name, so it can stand for any male person.

clue.text: Analysis of collapse

definitions.meaning: analysis as in a detailed itemised account

explanation.definitionFit: A detailed itemisation and a sudden failure, mechanical or mental, share this word.

clue.text: Disparaging remark when somebody detains one

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: detains signals that the word for somebody holds another piece inside it

parts.note: somebody is a person
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A slur uttered when someone keeps another person in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detains' puts I inside PERSON.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur or derogatory comment attacking someone's character is a slanderous remark of this kind.

clue.text: Visual aid overseas, so to speak

definitions.text: Visual aid overseas, so to speak

parts.words: Visual aid overseas, so to speak
parts.note: read as a viewing device used to look over the seas, as from a submarine below the surface

explanation.surface: Teaching aids used abroad, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overseas' suggests abroad, but read it as 'over seas': the device lets a submerged submarine look out over the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine's tube with mirrors gives a view above the surface, a sighting instrument.

clue.text: Winter sports person keeping fish in freezer?

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the freezer word has the fish placed within it

parts.note: an icer is something that freezes or ices
skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A winter athlete who stores fish in the deep-freeze.
explanation.walkthrough: Freezer reads as the appliance, but here it is anything that ices, and the fish is the flat skate, not a goldfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gliding on blades over a frozen rink takes part in a winter sport.

clue.text: Lively party in joint with drink

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A lively party held in a pub with drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Joint looks like a pub or a cannabis cigarette, but it is the leg's joint; a knees-up is a British term for a riotous party.
explanation.definitionFit: A boisterous British celebration with dancing is named for the high-kicking it involves.

clue.text: In another month the heating unit arrives

indicators.note: In signals that the answer lies concealed inside the following words

explanation.surface: The heating comes on when the next month starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to letters inside 'another month'; 'the' and 'arrives' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of heat formerly used in British gas bills, equal to 100,000 British thermal units.

clue.text: Crush racket involved in crooked let

indicators.note: involved in signals that the racket is placed inside the jumbled word
crooked means bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ramp is British slang for a swindle or racket

explanation.surface: Stamping out a racket in a dishonest letting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' scrambles 'let' to TLE, which then wraps round the racket; RAMP is British slang for a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush underfoot is to stamp on something heavily.

clue.text: Rings of steel, perhaps, surrounding low joints

definitions.text: Rings of steel, perhaps, surrounding low joints

parts.words: Rings of steel, perhaps, surrounding low joints
parts.note: read as metal bands, like fetters or jewellery, worn around the joints at the bottom of the legs

explanation.surface: Metal rings encircling joints low down, as on machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low joints' sounds like engineering, but it means the joints just above the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: These are bracelets or bands worn round the lowest leg joints, which steel fetters also encircle.

clue.text: What's needed to settle a raga, initially?

definitions.text: What's needed to settle a raga, initially?

parts.note: to settle is to sit

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of raga is used

explanation.surface: Asks what is needed to begin a piece of Indian music.
explanation.walkthrough: A raga is a melodic form in Indian classical music, played on the lute this clue's whole reading describes.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-necked Indian lute is the instrument a raga is classically played on.

clue.text: More relaxed passenger

definitions.meaning: more relaxed means looser, less taut
a passenger is someone in a team who does not pull their weight

explanation.definitionFit: Looser is the comparative of loose, and a shirker carried by colleagues is called a passenger.

clue.text: One of the colours, standard for army

definitions.meaning: the usual cloth for military uniforms

explanation.definitionFit: A dull yellowish-brown colour is also the standard fabric of army uniforms.

clue.text: One studies symbols on computer screen

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Someone examines the little pictures on a monitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' is an old word meaning to study closely.
explanation.definitionFit: The small pictures standing for programs and files on a desktop are its graphic images.

clue.text: Happened to agree to job

definitions.meaning: to agree to a job is to accept a position, taking one's place

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: accepting a post is taking a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurred is the idiomatic meaning, while accepting a post is literally taking a position.

clue.text: Spur a person (whether good or bad)

definitions.meaning: to spur is to urge on
an old-fashioned word for a person, as in 'good sort' or 'bad lot'

explanation.walkthrough: A 'good egg' and a 'bad egg' are old-fashioned British terms for a decent or a rotten person.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone on is to goad them, and a person is a 'good' or 'bad' one in old slang.

clue.text: The old name for money out East

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: The traditional term for currency in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: YE is a mock-old spelling of 'the', as in 'Ye Olde Tea Shoppe'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the currency of Japan, a country in the Far East.

clue.text: Maintaining a separation

parts.note: per means a, as in 'ten pounds a head'
severing is cutting apart, a separation

explanation.surface: Keeping a separation in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' in the sense of 'each' gives PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping on steadily with something despite difficulty is persisting, which is what maintaining can mean.
